title: Is it Possible to Get New Teeth in a Day? Explore the All-on-4 Dental Implant Procedure
excerpt: New teeth in a day? Is it possible? This article explores the all-on-4 teeth in a day dental implant procedure, highlighting the benefits and risk factors.
body:
Are you tired of dealing with missing teeth or uncomfortable dentures? Imagine waking up and having a brand-new set of permanent teeth in just one day. This dream can now become a reality with the innovative dental procedure known as “teeth-in-a-day.” If you’re curious about how this process works and whether it’s right for you, keep reading.

What Are Teeth in a Day?

Teeth in a day, also referred colloquially to as “teeth in a hour” or “same day teeth” or as “same-day dental implants” or “immediate dental implants”, is a cutting-edge dental procedure that allows patients to receive a full set of new teeth in a single day. Unlike traditional dental implant treatments that can take several months to complete, teeth in a day offers a quicker and more convenient solution for full mouth restorations.

Exploring the All-on-4 Dental Implant Process

What Is a Dental Implant?

A dental implant is a titanium post that is surgically permanently implanted into the jaw bone to serve as a replacement for a missing tooth root. This post provides a stable foundation for a crown, bridge, or denture, restoring both the function and appearance of natural teeth.

How Are Teeth in a Day Different?

The traditional dental implant process involves multiple visits to the dentist over several months. However, with the teeth in a day procedure, everything is completed in just one appointment. This means that patients can leave the dental office with a beautiful new smile on the same day as their surgery.

What Can I Expect During Surgery?

During the teeth in a day procedure, any diseased teeth are removed, and dental implants are placed directly into the jawbone. Thanks to advancements in dental technology, this process can often be completed with less trauma and discomfort compared to traditional implant surgeries. Generally, only four implants made from titanium are used for each arch in a minimally invasive procedure allowing the surgeon to work with the available bone in your jaw, without the need of bone grafting, in a technique called “all-on-4 dental implants“.

Photo Credit: Nobel Biocare

These implants act as a foundation which allows the placement of a fixed set of teeth, that are indistinguishable from natural teeth. Thanks to an in-house 3D intraoral scanner, printer and software technology, a complete digital impression of the patient’s mouth is taken to fully map the teeth and gums. With this data then, a custom made temporary denture, also called temporary bridge, is 3-D printed, painted in the gum area, cured in a light cure box for about one minute and it is ready for the patient immediately.

All-on-4 Dental Implants Prosthesis

Benefits of Teeth in a Day

1. Immediate Results

One of the most significant advantages of the same day teeth procedure is the immediate results it offers. Instead of waiting months for your final restoration, you can enjoy a brand-new smile with renewed function right away.

2. Reduced Healing Period

Because teeth in a day eliminates the need for multiple surgeries and lengthy healing periods, patients can return to their normal activities much sooner. This means less time spent recovering and more time enjoying life with your new set of teeth.

3. Enhanced Confidence

Missing teeth can take a toll on your self-esteem and confidence. With teeth in a day, you can regain your smile and your confidence in just one day, allowing you to feel great about your appearance once again.

Is Teeth-in-a-Day Implant Treatment Right for You?

Here is a short – non exhaustive – list of indications for this surgical procedure.

Are You Missing Teeth?

Teeth in a day is an excellent option for individuals who are missing one or more teeth and are looking for a permanent solution for tooth replacement.

Do You have Adequate Bone Density?

If you have been missing teeth for a long time, your bone density might have regressed over time in the mandible (lower jaw) or maxilla (upper jaw). Your surgeon will be able to verify this through 3D dental x-rays and other software technology. Depending on the available bone density in the upper jaw, the surgeon might recommend the placement zygomatic implants, an advanced technique particularly useful in those with severe bone loss in their upper jaw.

Do You Want Immediate Results?

If you want to avoid the long waiting periods associated with traditional dental implant procedures, teeth in a day may be the perfect solution for you.

Are You Looking for a Convenient Option?

For busy individuals who don’t have time for multiple dental appointments, teeth in a day offers a convenient and time-saving alternative.

What Factors Play a Role in the Success of Same-day Dental Implants?

The dental and medical history of the patient is critical for the success of the surgery. Here is a – non exhaustive – list of factors that add risk to the success of the procedure.

  • Heavy smoking: Smokers must note they are two and a half times more likely to experience failure than non-smokers. The relative risk of implant failure is significantly higher in patients who smoke 20 cigarettes or more per day compared to nonsmokers. Furthermore, heavy smokers have significantly higher chances of post-surgery infection rates.
  • Gum disease: Those who suffer from gum disease will need to have the condition successfully treated prior to proceeding with implants. A good gum health is pivotal for the success rate of any dental placement procedure.
  • Diabetes: Patients with diabetes usually have co-morbidities (existing medical conditions) and have, therefore, a higher risk of post-op infection as this condition slows down the body’s ability to fight infections.
  • Oral hygiene: It is important the patient understands the importance of good oral hygiene and is able to undertake daily brushing and flossing using correct techniques prior to the placement of implants.

Conclusion: A New Smile in Just One Day is Possible.

The teeth in a day technology has revolutionised the field of dentistry, offering a fast, convenient, and permanent solution for tooth replacement. Whether you’re missing one tooth or an entire arch, this innovative procedure can provide you with a brand-new smile in just one day. If you’re tired of dealing with missing teeth, pain or uncomfortable dentures, schedule a consultation with your dental practitioner to see if teeth in a day is right for you.

title: Why Wisdom Teeth Removal Before Age 25 May Be Easier than Later
excerpt: Wisdom teeth removal before the age of 25 is recommended in certain cases before it may cause any significant problems.
body:
Removal of a troublesome wisdom tooth is a very common procedure in dentistry, however this procedure is often left too late and can cause serious complications. In this article, we explain what to pay attention to and why intervening early is important. Older adults may require longer procedure and/or face complications.

What are Wisdom Teeth?

Wisdom teeth is the most common term behind third set of molars. These teeth do not erupt through the gums usually until people are in their late teens or early 20s. There are four wisdom teeth in total but not every person has all of them fully formed.

What are Impacted Wisdom Teeth?

Sometimes there is not enough space at the back of the jaw for a wisdom tooth to come through, so this can become “impacted” which is a fancy dental term to say that the tooth is partially or fully trapped in your gums in different positions and angles. Some impacted third molars will never cause any issues, they just stay buried in their position. However, other impacted wisdom teeth may cause sever issues, including infection in the surrounding gum tissue.

Here are Some Issues Troublesome Wisdom Teeth Can Create

Impacted wisdom teeth can cause the following issues:

  • Pain: in the neighbouring teeth caused by the pressure of the wisdom tooth, or cause by an infection.
  • Infection: particularly at the top of the tooth when this is about to erupt.
  • Cyst: this is a sac of fluid that can form around the wisdom tooth (often unerupted) and may displace it. It may destroy the bone and damage other surrounding teeth and gums.
  • Ulcer: this can happen when a wisdom tooth in the upper jawbone pushes sideways out of the gum and rubbing against he inside of the cheek.
  • Resorption Cavity: this happens when an impacted tooth pushes towards and hits the molar next to it causing bone damage to both teeth. Luckily this is not very common.
  • A food trap: when food becomes trapped when food becomes trapped between a wisdom tooth and its adjacent molar increasing the risk of tooth decay.

What is the Best Age to Remove Your Wisdom Teeth?

Removing the wisdom teeth, particularly, if any pain has been noticed, should be done as early as possible. Having such problematic teeth removed between ages of 17 and 25 is recommended because the roots of the wisdom teeth have not formed totally, and the bone surrounding the tooth is softer making the extraction process easier.

Indications for Early Wisdom Teeth Extraction

The surgical extraction of wisdom teeth is indicated (recommended) for the following reasons:

  1. The concerned tooth or gum area has started to cause pain
  2. There is not enough room in the mouth for the tooth to push through
  3. Orthodontic work (braces) may be needed as space is needed
  4. When the other molars around the impacted tooth need to be protected
  5. Last, but one of the most important reasons is when the impacted wisdom tooth in the lower jaw is close to major nerves like the inferior alveolar nerve or the lingual nerve which may complicate the extraction process.

Your dentist or oral surgeon may need to take x-rays to determine the need to remove wisdom teeth.

Delaying wisdom teeth removal is often regretted when not occurred in the teenage years.

The Wisdom Teeth Removal Procedure

Usually, a general dentist will refer patients to an oral surgeon for wisdom teeth extraction procedures. The surgeon will use local anaesthetic, general anaesthetic, or sedation therapy to make the patient comfortable depending on the individual clinical case. During the procedure the surgeon will then make an incision (cut) to open the gums and a small portion of the bone to be able to extract the impacted tooth. The tooth may have to be divided into small sections to be able to be extracted safely. Lastly, the incision is closed with stitches that will dissolve in a few days or may need a follow-up appointment to be removed.
